QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_2

question.text: 'Saraswati Credit Opportunities Fund' is debating whether to set itself up as a trust or an LLP. The sponsor group wants the manager to have maximum ring-fencing of liability. From the manager's standpoint, why does the trust structure best achieve this?

answer.text: A trust is registered with the Registrar of Companies, which gives the manager statutory immunity under the Companies Act, 2013.
A trust structure allows the manager to retain all fiduciary powers without any delegation from the trustee.

A trust structure ring-fences the manager's liability because the manager is only a counterparty service provider to the AIF, unlike also being on the board of directors (company) or a designated partner (LLP).
A trust structure exempts the manager from the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012 fiduciary duty obligations.

explanation.text: The Logic: In a trust-form AIF, the investment manager enters into the IMA as a counterparty service provider to the AIF. It is NOT on the board of directors of a company AIF or a designated partner of an LLP AIF. That counterparty-only role is what ring-fences the manager's fiduciary and breach-of-fund-document liability from that of the AIF, and is the reason most Indian AIFs are trusts. The Trap: Trusts are registered with the Sub-Registrar (not ROC — that is LLP/company). The manager retains fiduciary duty regardless of form — that never goes away. SEBI (AIF) Regulations apply equally across all three forms. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C Manager tests the same liability ring-fencing concept across all forms; XXI-B Portfolio Manager has a different setup because listed-securities PM is typically a company-form entity with a different liability profile.
